sections.heading: 1. Timing and grip
lines: ① Deeper work 1–2 days before a hard session.
② Skip deep massage the morning of a race.
③ Hold the paddle or handle lightly.
④ Forearm stretch 20 sec × 3 after sessions.

caption:
Lulu kayaks every weekend, and his back and forearms are feeling it. 🚣

Rowing and paddling load the lats, forearms, upper back and hip flexors over thousands of strokes. Remedial massage can help ease that tightness, but it won't replace sleep, food, a sensible training load or strength work.

Hybi's tips: schedule deeper work a day or two before hard sessions, skip it the morning of a race, and keep a relaxed grip on the paddle.

Sharp rib pain, pain that worsens each session or tingling hands is worth a physio assessment first. Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physio can tailor each session. Book online via the link in bio.
